default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-348.title: Frozen day-range micro-break fade
E-348.hypothesis: When neither the session high nor the session low has moved for a long time, the day's range is established and both edges are held by responsive traders; a short-term break inside that frozen range reaches no level with stops behind it and the small breaker is leaned back by liquidity providers, so fade it.

E-349.title: Multi-day value micro-break fade
E-349.hypothesis: When the price sits near the mean price of the last 20 sessions (inside k multi-day sds), it is at the swing traders' accepted value: they sell above and buy below it and no multi-day initiator is pushing; short-term breaks there are local pushes the multi-day holders absorb, so fade them.

E-350.title: Post-heavy-volume-session micro-break fade
E-350.hypothesis: A session that traded far more contracts than the 20-session norm was an event day whose large orders were executed then; the next session is digestion by dealers rebuilding inventory with no parent order left to work, so its short-term breaks are faded (yesterday's volume, not its range or close).

E-351.title: Inside-noise-band micro-break fade
E-351.hypothesis: Moves from the open that stay inside the average absolute move for this minute (the Zarattini/Aziz noise area) are the territory of liquidity providers; while price is still inside that band, a break of the recent high/low is noise they lean back, so fade it (the complement regime of following an exit, E-128).

E-352.title: VWAP-launch break follow
E-352.hypothesis: A short-term break made soon after the price touched the session VWAP, on the VWAP side it now trades, starts from the day's average cost: benchmark buyers who filled at value hold the inventory behind it and nobody is trapped above, so the push away from value carries; follow the break (not the touch-hold of E-079).

E-353.title: Daily-reversal-regime micro-break fade
E-353.hypothesis: When the last 15 daily close-to-close returns are negatively autocorrelated, each day undoes the last: the multi-day market is run by mean-reverting swing traders rather than trend flow; in that regime intraday short-term breaks also lack follow-through and are faded (daily-scale autocorrelation, not intraday).

E-354.title: Volume-drought week micro-break fade
E-354.hypothesis: When the last 5 sessions traded clearly fewer contracts than the 20-session norm, institutional participants are away (holidays, waiting for an event) and the book is run by local market makers; short-term breaks then have no size behind them and are leaned back, so fade them.

E-355.title: Compact-value session micro-break fade
E-355.hypothesis: When today's volume-weighted dispersion of trade around the session VWAP is small next to its usual value at this minute, the day's volume is concentrated at one value that both sides accept; a short-term break away from that compact value is a probe the value traders return, so fade it.

E-356.title: Previous-hour VWAP hold after value migration
E-356.hypothesis: When the last completed clock hour's VWAP stepped well above the hour before, value is migrating up and the last hour's buyers hold inventory at that VWAP; the first bar that dips to it and closes back above meets their defence, so buy (mirror for a downward step).

E-357.title: Unfilled gap-zone micro-break fade
E-357.hypothesis: While price trades inside a meaningful overnight gap that has not been filled (between yesterday's close and today's open), it is in a zone with no inventory from either session, where gap-fill traders and gap holders both trade responsively; short-term breaks inside it are absorbed, so fade them.
